title: List vs Set vs Map
question: What is the difference between List, Set, and Map in Java? When do you use each?
seoKeywords: List vs Set vs Map java
when to use List Set Map java

title: fail-fast vs fail-safe Iterators
question: What is the difference between fail-fast and fail-safe iterators in Java?
searchIntent: fail-fast vs fail-safe iterator java interview
realWorldScenario: ArrayList iterator is fail-fast (throws CME on modification); CopyOnWriteArrayList iterator is fail-safe (iterates over a snapshot).

title: HashMap vs TreeMap Performance

seoKeywords: HashMap vs TreeMap time complexity java
O(1) vs O(log n) java map
searchIntent: HashMap TreeMap time complexity java interview
realWorldScenario: HashMap O(1) for lookups vs TreeMap O(log n) — prefer HashMap unless sorted traversal is required.

title: ArrayList vs Array
question: What is the difference between an Array and an ArrayList in Java?
searchIntent: when to use array vs ArrayList java
realWorldScenario: Arrays have fixed size and can hold primitives; ArrayList is dynamic and holds objects only.

title: Stack vs Queue
question: What is the difference between a Stack and a Queue in Java? Give real-world examples of each.
realWorldScenario: Stack (LIFO): browser history navigation. Queue (FIFO): print spooler, task scheduler.

title: Synchronized Collections vs Concurrent Collections
question: What is the difference between synchronized collections (Collections.synchronizedList) and concurrent collections (CopyOnWriteArrayList, ConcurrentHashMap)?
searchIntent: synchronized vs concurrent collection java interview
realWorldScenario: Synchronized collections lock the whole object; concurrent collections use finer-grained locking for better throughput.

title: Iterator vs ListIterator
question: What is the difference between Iterator and ListIterator in Java?
realWorldScenario: ListIterator allows backward traversal and element replacement — useful when scanning a list bidirectionally.
